message.reasoning_content:
The vendor is Precision Parts Ltd.

This is a classic payment redirect fraud pattern. The email requests updated bank details and a new remittance account. The sender domain differs from the vendor name. The document itself contains the new account information.

The vendor name matches the known vendor. The remit-to party is the same bank, not a different entity. This does not satisfy the vendor_change criteria.

The sender domain does not match the vendor name exactly. This could be a vendor_change signal. The similarity to the vendor name is only partial.

The vendor master has no aliases. The payment redirect signal will cite the bank change text and subject line. The sender domain may also be flagged as a vendor change.

The signal level is high. The document contains no pressure language or instruction injection. I am now selecting exact quotes from the invoice text.

The payment redirect signal will cite the sentence about changed bank details. The vendor change signal is still being selected.

The vendor_change signal will cite the sender address "From: billing@precision-parts-payments.com". The vendor master has no aliases for this domain. This confirms the payment instruction does not originate from the known vendor.
